1 1.

The present complaint has been filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,
1954 (herein after referred to as PFA Act), alleging that the accused has violated the provisions of the PFA Act and Rules.

2. As per the complaint, on 04.11.2010 at about 06:00 PM, Food Inspector (herein after referred to as 'FI') Ms. Usha Kiran, under the supervision/directions of Sh. Pardeep Baijal, SDM/LHA visited the premises of M/s Bansal Corner, 22, Central Market, Ashok Vihar, Phase-I, Delhi-110052.
Accused Adesh Bansal was found conducting the business at the said shop, having stored various food articles including "Chocopie" for sale for human consumption.
A sample consisting of 3x336g (12 packets) of "Chocopie" having label declaration 'ready for sale' was taken for inspection.

Vide report dated 08.12.2010, the PA reported that the sample was misbranded because there is CC No:-
44284/2016 DA (FSO) v. Adesh Bansal Page No. 2 of 14 violation of Rule 32(c) (iii), Rule 32(i) and Rule 64-BB of PFA Act and Rules, 1955.

sentences.text: The public analyst has also reported in his above stated report regarding label, without declaration of importer's address, expiration date given as 15 months from production and flavour declared as vanilla (artificial).
However the sample was not adulterated.
Hence, the present complaint was filed.

3. Since the complaint was filed by a public servant in writing, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 24.03.2011.
4.
On appearing before the Court, accused was admitted to bail and provided with copy of complaint.

He was served with notice under Section 251 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 (hereinafter referred to as 'Cr.P.C') on 22.07.2011 for offences punishable under Section of PFA Act and Rules, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
COMPLAINANT EVIDENCE 5.
At the trial, the complainant department i.e. the prosecution examined four witnesses in support of its case.
Sh. Pradeep, Retired SDM/LHA, Government of NCT of Delhi was examined as PW-1.

PW-1 in his examination-in-chief stated CC No:- 44284/2016 DA (FSO) v. Adesh Bansal Page No. 3 of 14 that after lifting of sample, it was divided into three parts as per procedure prescribed under the PFA Act and Rules and separately packed and sealed.

As per PW-1 on 06.11.2010, one counterpart of the sample was deposited with the Public Analyst (PA) and remaining two counterparts were deposited with the LHA.
As per PW-1, based on the report of PA, investigation was carried out by the Food Inspector on his instructions of the LHA.
As per the witness after obtaining due sanction of the Director, PFA the present complaint was filed against the accused persons.

PW-1 was duly cross-examined by counsel for accused.
During cross-examination PW-1 could not recollect whether the manufacturing date and MRP was mentioned on the label of the sample commodity or not.
He admitted that accused was not the manufacturer of the sample commodity and was only selling the sample commodity.
7. Ms. Usha Rani, Food Safety Officer, who was part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings was examined as PW-2.
PW-2 deposed on similar lines as PW-1 and corroborated his version.
She deposed that during sample proceedings she tried to associate customers, passers-by and neighbours but none came forward and hence FA Manhor Lal joined as a witness.
PW-2 was cross examined by counsel for the accused and admitted that the sample commodity was originally in a sealed packet when it was lifted.
8. Sh. O. P. S. Ahlawat, Designated Officer was examined as PW- 3.

He deposed that he carried out further investigation with respect to constitution of M/s Bansal Corner and relied upon the following documents i.e.

9. He also relied upon the documents Ex. PW 1/G and Ex. PW 1/H.

However, PW-3 could not be cross-examined by the accused as he had subsequently expired and his name was dropped from the Complainant vs Adesh Bansal on 26 July, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22060283/

sentences.text: 10. Sh. S. M. Bhardwaj, Food Analyst was examined as PW-4.
He deposed that on 06.11.2010, he received a sample of chocopie in sealed condition bearing code number 61/1041/97/2010 for analysis.
As per PW-4 he conducted chemical analysis of the said sample and prepared his report dated 08.12.2010 which is Ex. PW 1/F.
He also deposed that after analysis it was found that the sample was misbranded because there was violation of Rule 32 c(iii), Rule 32(i) and Rule 65-BB of PFA Act and Rule 1955.
The witness was not cross-examined despite opportunity.
11. No other witness was examined and PE was closed.
Thereafter, all the incriminating evidence was put to the accused and his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. was recorded.
Accused also stated that several customer were present at the time of inspection but none was asked to join the investigation.
He CC No:- 44284/2016 DA (FSO) v. Adesh Bansal Page No. 6 of 14 stated that he was neither the manufacturer nor the sample was packed or any impression of branding was done by him.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further stated that he had provided the bills from where he had purchased the sample to the officials but they had not investigated further on the same issue.
He also stated that he is the owner of the departmental store where items come in a packed form and he had sold the same to the customers.
No evidence in defence was led by the accused and the matter was listed for final arguments.

12. Ld. SPP for the complainant has argued that the complainant has been able to prove its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt, as all the witnesses have supported the case and there is no contradiction in their testimony.
It is submitted that the accused has failed to rebut the findings as given by the PA.
13. Counsel for the accused on the other hand argued that accused is neither the manufacturer or packer of the food sample and is only a retailer of the food article.
He further argued that the quantity of food article was purchased in bulk and the label of the food sample has not been placed on record.
It was further argued by Ld.
Counsel for accused that accused had no knowledge of the violation complained of in the present case.

sentences.text: Page No. 7 of 14 14.
I have heard the arguments advanced by Ld. SPP for the Complainant and Ld. Defence Counsel for the accused persons and have carefully perused the material available on record.
15. In the present case, accused has not questioned the spot sample proceedings conducted by the food officials, as deposed by the PW-1 and PW-2.
It is not his case that sample proceedings were not conducted as deposed or were conducted in any improper manner.
It is also not the defence of the accused that the commodity in question as lifted by the food officials did not belong to the accused.
16. It is neither disputed by the accused that the sampled commodity was a food article and covered under the PFA Act and Rules.
It is not his case that the sampled commodity did not fall in the category of food or was not meant for human consumption.

Complainant vs Adesh Bansal on 26 July, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22060283/

sentences.text: Further, there is no dispute that the food article as lifted in the present case would fall within the meaning of "package" as per section 2(x) of PFA Act.

As per this definition, a box, a bottle, a casket,
tin, barrel, case, sack, bag, wrapper or 'other thing' in which an article of food is placed or packed is included.

Since the food article in question was placed and packed in boxes and CC No:-
44284/2016 DA (FSO) v. Adesh Bansal Page No. 8 of 14 duly sealed and safely packed, the final packet would definitely be a 'package' under the Act.

entities.text:
CC No:-
44284/2016 DA (FSO) v. Adesh Bansal
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, the said package can be conveniently be called as a prepackaged product within the meaning of Rule 2(t) of the PFA Rules.
When an article is packaged or made up in advance and is ready to be offered to the consumer, it would be a prepackaged product.
It is clear and rather an admitted position that the food article in question had been made up in advance and was ready to be offered to the consumer.
It is nowhere the case of the accused that the food article was yet to be processed further or was yet to be labelled further before being offered to the consumer.

It is nowhere the stand of the accused that there were some blank columns on the label of the containers which were yet to be filled by them or the vendor before being actually offered to the consumer for sale.

18. Once it is so established that the food article was a prepackaged food, there is no reason why the Packing and Labelling standards, as prescribed in Part-VII of the PFA Rules would not apply to it.

19. Further misbranded is defined under the act as follows:-
"misbranded" - an article of food shall be deemed to be misbranded- (a) ****

(k) if it is not labelled in accordance with the requirement of this Act or rule made thereunder...."

5 20.

Also, Section 7 of The Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 read as under:-
Section 7. Prohibitions of manufacture, sale, etc., of certain articles of food.-
As per the complaint, the label has been reproduced by the FI on the Notice in Form-VI prepared at the spot which is Ex. PW- 1/B.
This fact has not been disputed by the defence.
It is nowhere the stand of the accused that the FI had incorrectly mentioned or incompletely mentioned the contents of the label on this form.

No such allegation has been levelled at any stage of the trial including the prosecution evidence, statement of the CC No:- 44284/2016 DA (FSO) v. Adesh Bansal Page No. 10 of 14 accused person or by defence evidence.

sentences.text: 22. Perusal of Form-VI would show that the label of the product mentioned the name of the product as "Chocopie" (ready for sale) 3x336 g. (12 packets) of originally sealed card board boxes of chocopie of same B. N. bearing following lable declaration taken as such.

Chocopie new quality 12 packs Net Wet: 336 g, ingrediets Wheat Flour, Sugar, Glucose, Agar-Agar, Shortening (palm oil), corn starch,
salt, sodium Bicarbonate, Cocoa powder, Milk powder, vanilla (artificial).

, Production date:
09.09.2010, Manufactured by Mite Enterprises SDN, BDH (BN: 019041), Perak, Malaysia, India Distributors, K. K. International, Mumbai, India, Expiration Date: 15 months from date of production, Store in a cool place.
23. It is nowhere the stand of the accused persons that some other relevant declarations were also there on the label which were not reproduced by the FI, deliberately or intentionally.

No attempt has been made by the accused persons to summon the labels from the office of the PA or the other counterparts from the office of the LHA to compare the same with Form-VI i.e. Ex. PW 1/B in case they had any such defence.

24. The relevant rule under the PFA Rule are as follow:-

6 CC No:- 44284/2016

DA (FSO) v. Adesh Bansal Page No. 11 of 14 25. Rule 32 of The Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 read as under:
Rule 32. Every prepackaged food to carry a label:-
(a) ****
(b) ****
(c) ****
(i) ****
(ii) ****
(iii) Where an article of food is imported into India, the package of food shall also carry the name and complete address of the importer in India:
26. Rule 32 (i) read as follows:-
(i) the month and year in capital letters upto which the product is best for consumption, in the following manner, namely:-
" BEST BEFORE ............... MONTHS AND YEAR"
"BEST BEFORE ............... MONTHS FROM PACKAGING"
"BEST BEFORE ............... MONTHS FROM MANUFACTURE"
OR [For "BEST BEFORE UPTO MONTH AND YEAR ..............." the period upto OR and BEST BEFORE WITHIN ............... MONTHS FROM inclusive THE DATE OF PACKAGING/MANUFACTURE" of 1st September, 2001]
27. Rule 64-BB. Extraneous addition of flavoring agents to be mentioned on the label:-
" Where an extraneous flavouring agent has been added to any article of food, there shall be written just beneath the list of ingredients on the label, attached to any package of food so flavored, a statement in capital letters as below:-
CONTAINS ADDED FLAVOUR (specify type of flavoring agent as per rule 63) CC No:- 44284/2016 DA (FSO) v. Adesh Bansal Page No. 12 of 14 Complainant vs Adesh Bansal on 26 July, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22060283/
7 28.

The careful reading of the PF report i.e. Ex. PW 1/F clearly shows that the sample was misbranded because it did not declare importers address, expiry date was not as per prescribed format under Rule 32(i) and was mentioned as 15 months from production and flavour was not mentioned as per Rule 64-BB.
No evidence has been led on behalf of the defence to show that there was no misbranding on behalf of the accused.
Therefore, the offence of misbranding is clearly established in the present case.

29. Further perusal of Ex. PW 1/B clearly shows that address of importer was not mentioned on the label and the expiry dateas well as the presence of flavoring agent is not mentioned in the manner as prescribed in the rules.
Further as per Ex. PW 3/A accused is the proprietor of firm namely M/s Bansal Corner, 22, Central Market, Ashok Vihar, Phase-I, as per record.

30. On bare reading of Section 7 of the Act, it is clear that the liability under the Act is absolute i.e.
there is total elimination of mens era.
So the liability of a person contravening any of the provision contained in Section 7 is an absolute liability and it does not depend upon the existence of any particular knowledge or intention.
CC No:- 44284/2016 DA (FSO) v. Adesh Bansal

32. In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, accused Adesh Bansal S/o Late Sh. S. N. Bansal is hereby convicted for the violation of provisions of Section 2 (ix) (k) r/w Rule 32(c)
(iii), Rule 32(i) and Rule 64-BB r/w Section 7 of the PFA Act and PFA Rules and punishable U/s 16(1) (a) of the PFA Act, 1954.
33.
